**2B.4 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Best-supported reading: there is no evidence in the 2024 record that Srettha directed Thai military operations in a way that violated civilian protection, necessity, or proportionality. The evidence instead points to border-management, humanitarian access, and diplomatic de-escalation around Myanmar. Direct evidence on prisoner treatment is absent.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 18, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand backed immediate restraint, cessation of violence, defusing tensions, and humanitarian access. This is the clearest evidence relevant to civilian protection and proportionality, because it favors restraint and humanitarian access over military escalation. | `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Thailand stresses the importance of upscaling humanitarian assistance along the Thai-Myanmar border at the Human Rights Council](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 4, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand emphasized humanitarian assistance, dialogue, reconciliation, and a peaceful, stable Myanmar. That is consistent with civilian-protection norms and with avoiding unnecessary force. | `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |

This is practical evidence of prioritizing civilian protection and humanitarian channels. | `2B.4`, `2B.1` |
| [Vice Foreign Minister Sihasak meets with Special Envoy of ASEAN Chair on Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/pr210424-2) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 24, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/pr210424-2 | Thailand and the ASEAN Chair’s Special Envoy stressed de-escalation, cessation of hostilities, and maintaining ASEAN centrality. This supports a proportional, restraint-first approach rather than force-first military conduct. | `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |

That is a controlled, coordinated response rather than an indiscriminate military operation. | `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Thailand working ‘relentlessly’ to solve Myanmar crisis - Srettha](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha) | Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News | May 24, 2024 | https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha | Srettha said Thailand was working to reduce spillover violence and end the Myanmar crisis. This is indirect but relevant evidence of a restraint-oriented posture. | `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |

**Search gap**

- I found no credible 2024 evidence of Thai military operations under Srettha that raised civilian-protection, prisoner-treatment, necessity, or proportionality concerns.
- I also found no direct evidence on prisoner treatment in a combat context, because the record does not show Thailand conducting a relevant military campaign in 2024.
- So the best-supported conclusion is limited but positive: the available record shows humanitarian access, restraint, and border coordination, not abusive or disproportionate military action.
